159: func (r controlledRuntime) StartRun(ctx context.Context, req runtimepkg.Request) (runtimepkg.Result, error) {
160: 	target := targetFromRuntimeRequest(req)
161: 	correlation := runcontrol.Correlation{
162: 		ProductRunID:  boundedSafe(string(runcontrol.ParentRun(ctx))),
163: 		ProductTaskID: boundedSafe(req.TraceID),
164: 	}
165: 	snapshot, err := r.repository.Accept(ctx, runcontrol.Acceptance{
166: 		Target:        target,
167: 		Correlation:   correlation,
168: 		ProductStatus: "accepted",
169: 	})
170: 	if err != nil {
171: 		return runtimepkg.Result{}, fmt.Errorf("durable run acceptance failed: %w", err)
172: 	}
173: 	attempt, _, err := r.repository.Claim(ctx, runcontrol.Claim{
174: 		RunID: snapshot.RunID, Owner: r.owner, Lease: runControlLease, Correlation: correlation,
175: 	})
176: 	if err != nil {
177: 		return runtimepkg.Result{}, fmt.Errorf("durable run ownership failed: %w", err)
178: 	}
179: 	fence := runcontrol.Fence{
180: 		RunID: snapshot.RunID, AttemptID: attempt.ID, OwnerID: r.owner.ID,
181: 		FencingGeneration: attempt.FencingGeneration,
182: 	}
183: 
184: 	runCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
185: 	defer cancel()
186: 	req.Metadata = cloneRuntimeMetadata(req.Metadata)
187: 	req.Metadata["run_control_run_id"] = string(snapshot.RunID)
188: 	configuredOnEvent := req.OnEvent
189: 	var eventMu sync.Mutex
190: 	var persistenceErr error
191: 	var progressKey string
192: 	var progressCommittedAt time.Time
193: 	var progressOmitted uint64
194: 	var progressOmittedFirst time.Time
195: 	var progressOmittedLast time.Time
196: 	setPersistenceErr := func(value error) {
197: 		eventMu.Lock()
198: 		defer eventMu.Unlock()
199: 		if persistenceErr == nil {
200: 			persistenceErr = value
201: 			cancel()
202: 		}
203: 	}
204: 	req.OnEvent = func(event runtimepkg.Event) {
205: 		eventMu.Lock()
206: 		defer eventMu.Unlock()
207: 		if persistenceErr != nil {
208: 			return
209: 		}
210: 		draft := runtimeEventDraft(req, event)
211: 		eventAt := event.Time.UTC()
212: 		if eventAt.IsZero() {
213: 			eventAt = time.Now().UTC()
214: 		}
215: 		// Content-aware coalescing: only collapse identical progress payloads within the window.
216: 		// Reasoning/text deltas and tool calls have distinct payload hashes and will not coalesce.
217: 		hash := payloadHash(draft.Payload)
218: 		key := string(draft.Type) + "\x00" + draft.Stage + "\x00" + draft.Task + "\x00" + hash
219: 		elapsed := eventAt.Sub(progressCommittedAt)
220: 		if draft.Type == runcontrol.EventProgress && key == progressKey && elapsed >= 0 && elapsed < runcontrol.ProgressCoalesceWindow {
221: 			if progressOmitted == 0 {
222: 				progressOmittedFirst = eventAt
223: 			}
224: 			progressOmitted++
225: 			progressOmittedLast = eventAt
226: 			return
227: 		}
228: 		if progressOmitted > 0 {
229: 			if draft.Omission == nil {
230: 				draft.Omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced"}
231: 			}
232: 			draft.Omission.Count += progressOmitted
233: 			draft.Omission.FirstAt = &progressOmittedFirst
234: 			draft.Omission.LastAt = &progressOmittedLast
235: 			progressOmitted = 0
236: 		}
237: 		if _, _, appendErr := appendRunEventWithRetry(runCtx, r.repository, fence, draft); appendErr != nil {
238: 			persistenceErr = fmt.Errorf("persist runtime event: %w", appendErr)
239: 			cancel()
240: 			return
241: 		}
242: 		if draft.Type == runcontrol.EventProgress {
243: 			progressKey = key
244: 			progressCommittedAt = eventAt
245: 		}
246: 		if configuredOnEvent != nil {
247: 			configuredOnEvent(event)
248: 		}
249: 	}
250: 
251: 	controlDone := make(chan struct{})
252: 	go func() {
253: 		defer close(controlDone)
254: 		ticker := time.NewTicker(runcontrol.OwnerTickInterval)
255: 		defer ticker.Stop()
256: 		lastHeartbeat := time.Now()
257: 		lastReconcile := time.Now()
258: 		for {
259: 			select {
260: 			case <-runCtx.Done():
261: 				return
262: 			case now := <-ticker.C:
263: 				snapshot, err := r.repository.Snapshot(runCtx, fence.RunID)
264: 				if err != nil {
265: 					if runCtx.Err() != nil {
266: 						return
267: 					}
268: 					setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("poll durable run control: %w", err))
269: 					return
270: 				}
271: 				if snapshot.Cancellation.State == runcontrol.CancellationRequested {
272: 					if _, _, err := r.repository.AcknowledgeCancellation(runCtx, fence); err != nil {
273: 						setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("acknowledge durable cancellation: %w", err))
274: 						return
275: 					}
276: 					cancel()
277: 					return
278: 				}
279: 				if now.Sub(lastHeartbeat) >= runcontrol.HeartbeatInterval {
280: 					if _, err := r.repository.Heartbeat(runCtx, fence, runControlLease); err != nil {
281: 						if runCtx.Err() != nil {
282: 							return
283: 						}
284: 						setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("persist owner heartbeat: %w", err))
285: 						return
286: 					}
287: 					lastHeartbeat = now
288: 				}
289: 				if now.Sub(lastReconcile) >= runcontrol.ReconciliationInterval {
290: 					if _, err := r.repository.Reconcile(runCtx, runcontrol.NativeProcessProbe{}, runcontrol.ReconcileOptions{}); err != nil {
291: 						if runCtx.Err() != nil {
292: 							return
293: 						}
294: 						setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("reconcile durable runs: %w", err))
295: 						return
296: 					}
297: 					lastReconcile = now
298: 				}
299: 			}
300: 		}
301: 	}()
302: 	result, runErr := r.base.StartRun(runCtx, req)
303: 	eventMu.Lock()
304: 	if persistenceErr == nil && progressOmitted > 0 {
305: 		_, _, appendErr := appendRunEventWithRetry(runCtx, r.repository, fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{
306: 			Type: runcontrol.EventOmission,
307: 			Omission: &runcontrol.Omission{
308: 				Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced", Count: progressOmitted,
309: 				FirstAt: &progressOmittedFirst, LastAt: &progressOmittedLast,
310: 			},
311: 		})
312: 		if appendErr != nil {
313: 			persistenceErr = fmt.Errorf("persist progress omission: %w", appendErr)
314: 		}
315: 	}
316: 	eventMu.Unlock()
317: 	cancel()
318: 	<-controlDone
319: 	eventMu.Lock()
320: 	persistErr := persistenceErr
321: 	eventMu.Unlock()
322: 	if persistErr != nil {
323: 		terminalCtx, terminalCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
324: 		_, _, terminalErr := proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(terminalCtx, r.repository, fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{
325: 			Outcome: runcontrol.TerminalPersistenceLost, Reason: "durable event persistence failed", ProposedBy: r.owner.ID,
326: 		})
327: 		terminalCancel()
328: 		if terminalErr != nil {
329: 			return result, errors.Join(persistErr, terminalErr)
330: 		}
331: 		return result, persistErr
332: 	}
333: 
334: 	outcome, reason := terminalOutcome(result, runErr, ctx)
335: 	terminalCtx, terminalCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
336: 	defer terminalCancel()
337: 	if _, _, err := proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(terminalCtx, r.repository, fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{
338: 		Outcome: outcome, Reason: reason, ProposedBy: r.owner.ID,
339: 	}); err != nil {
340: 		return result, errors.Join(runErr, fmt.Errorf("persist terminal run outcome: %w", err))
341: 	}
342: 	return result, runErr
343: }

345: func appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx context.Context, repository runcontrol.Repository, fence runcontrol.Fence, draft runcontrol.EventDraft) (runcontrol.Event, runcontrol.Snapshot, error) {
346: 	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
347: 	for {
348: 		event, snapshot, err := repository.Append(ctx, fence, draft)
349: 		if err == nil || !retryableRunControlError(err) || !time.Now().Before(deadline) {
350: 			return event, snapshot, err
351: 		}
352: 		if err := waitRunControlRetry(ctx, deadline); err != nil {
353: 			return runcontrol.Event{}, runcontrol.Snapshot{}, err
354: 		}
355: 	}
356: }
357: 
358: func proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(ctx context.Context, repository runcontrol.Repository, fence runcontrol.Fence, proposal runcontrol.TerminalProposal) (runcontrol.Snapshot, bool, error) {
359: 	for {
360: 		snapshot, won, err := repository.ProposeTerminal(ctx, fence, proposal)
361: 		if err == nil || !retryableRunControlError(err) {
362: 			return snapshot, won, err
363: 		}
364: 		if err := waitRunControlRetry(ctx, time.Now().Add(250*time.Millisecond)); err != nil {
365: 			return runcontrol.Snapshot{}, false, err
366: 		}
367: 	}
368: }

370: func retryableRunControlError(err error) bool {
371: 	return errors.Is(err, runcontrol.ErrUnavailable) || errors.Is(err, runcontrol.ErrBusy)
372: }
373: 
374: func waitRunControlRetry(ctx context.Context, deadline time.Time) error {
375: 	wait := time.Until(deadline)
376: 	if wait > 100*time.Millisecond {
377: 		wait = 100 * time.Millisecond
378: 	}
379: 	if wait <= 0 {
380: 		return context.DeadlineExceeded
381: 	}
382: 	timer := time.NewTimer(wait)
383: 	defer timer.Stop()
384: 	select {
385: 	case <-ctx.Done():
386: 		return ctx.Err()
387: 	case <-timer.C:
388: 		return nil
389: 	}
390: }

392: func targetFromRuntimeRequest(req runtimepkg.Request) runcontrol.Target {

394: 		Kind:      boundedSafe(req.PromptRef.OwnerKind),
395: 		Operation: boundedSafe(req.PromptRef.Purpose),
396: 		Project:   boundedSafe(req.Metadata["project"]),
397: 		Sprint:    boundedSafe(req.Metadata["sprint"]),
398: 		Study:     boundedSafe(req.Metadata["study"]),
399: 		Stage:     boundedSafe(req.Metadata["stage"]),
400: 		Task:      boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(req.Metadata["task"], req.Metadata["task.kind"], req.Metadata["coverage"])),

402: 	if target.Kind == "" {

404: 			target.Kind = "study"
405: 		} else if target.Sprint != "" {
406: 			target.Kind = "sprint"
407: 		} else {
408: 			target.Kind = "runtime"
409: 		}
410: 	}
411: 	if target.Operation == "" {
412: 		target.Operation = boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(target.Stage, req.Metadata["task.kind"], req.PromptRef.ID, "runtime"))
413: 	}
414: 	return target
415: }

417: func runtimeEventDraft(req runtimepkg.Request, event runtimepkg.Event) runcontrol.EventDraft {
418: 	eventType := runcontrol.EventProgress
419: 	lowerType := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(event.Type))
420: 	lowerKind := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(event.Kind))
421: 	switch lowerType {
422: 	case "warning", "warn", "error":
423: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventWarning
424: 	case "artifact", "file":
425: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventArtifact
426: 	case "finding":
427: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventFinding
428: 	case "message", "text", "output", "assistant_text", "reasoning_text", "reasoning", "content", "delta":
429: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventMessage
430: 	default:
431: 		// Kind-based fallback: reasoning and message kinds should be visible as message, not coalesced progress.
432: 		switch lowerKind {
433: 		case "message", "reasoning", "assistant", "assistant_text", "reasoning_text":
434: 			eventType = runcontrol.EventMessage
435: 		case "tool", "tool_use", "tool_call", "tool_call_update":
436: 			// Tools stay as progress but with distinct payload so coalescing can distinguish.
437: 			eventType = runcontrol.EventProgress
438: 		}
439: 	}
440: 	payload := map[string]string{
441: 		"runtime_event_id": boundedSafe(event.ID),
442: 		"runtime_run_id":   boundedSafe(event.RunID),
443: 		"session_id":       boundedSafe(event.SessionID),
444: 		"type":             boundedSafe(event.Type),
445: 		"kind":             boundedSafe(event.Kind),
446: 	}
447: 	if lowerKind == "tool" || lowerKind == "tool_use" || lowerKind == "tool_call" || lowerKind == "tool_call_update" {
448: 		captureToolObservation(payload, event.Payload)
449: 	}
450: 	// Preserve safe observable payload fields into durable storage for observability.
451: 	// Deny sensitive keys and truncate values to runcontrol-safe limits.
452: 	// Flatten one level of nesting so tool/action names buried in maps are surfaced as top-level payload keys
453: 	// that the run timeline JS expects (payload.tool, payload.action, payload.title, etc.).
454: 	for key, value := range event.Payload {
455: 		if isSensitivePayloadKey(key) {
456: 			continue
457: 		}
458: 		normalized := strings.TrimSpace(key)
459: 		if normalized == "" || len(normalized) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(normalized, "\x00\r\n") {
460: 			continue
461: 		}
462: 		if normalized == "type" || normalized == "kind" {
463: 			continue
464: 		}
465: 		if nested, ok := value.(map[string]any); ok {
466: 			for subKey, subVal := range nested {
467: 				if isSensitivePayloadKey(subKey) {
468: 					continue
469: 				}
470: 				subNorm := strings.TrimSpace(subKey)
471: 				if subNorm == "" || len(subNorm) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(subNorm, "\x00\r\n") {
472: 					continue
473: 				}
474: 				if _, exists := payload[subNorm]; exists {
475: 					continue
476: 				}
477: 				// Promote common observable sub-keys; namespace the rest to avoid collisions.
478: 				promote := map[string]bool{"tool": true, "title": true, "detail": true, "text": true, "delta": true, "content": true, "message": true, "action": true, "state": true, "status": true, "native_type": true, "line": true}
479: 				targetKey := subNorm
480: 				if !promote[subNorm] {
481: 					targetKey = normalized + "_" + subNorm
482: 					if len(targetKey) > 128 {
483: 						continue
484: 					}
485: 				}
486: 				if _, exists := payload[targetKey]; exists {
487: 					continue
488: 				}
489: 				str := payloadValueString(subVal)
490: 				if strings.TrimSpace(str) == "" {
491: 					continue
492: 				}
493: 				if len(payload) >= 30 {
494: 					break
495: 				}
496: 				payload[targetKey] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
497: 			}
498: 			// Also keep a compact stringified top-level for debugging if not promoted.
499: 			if len(payload) < 30 {
500: 				if _, exists := payload[normalized]; !exists {
501: 					str := payloadValueString(value)
502: 					if strings.TrimSpace(str) != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(str, "[map omitted") {
503: 						payload[normalized] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
504: 					}
505: 				}
506: 			}
507: 			continue
508: 		}
509: 		str := payloadValueString(value)
510: 		if strings.TrimSpace(str) == "" {
511: 			continue
512: 		}
513: 		if len(payload) >= 30 {
514: 			break
515: 		}
516: 		if _, exists := payload[normalized]; exists {
517: 			continue
518: 		}
519: 		payload[normalized] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
520: 	}
521: 	// Ensure the most useful display keys are always present even if nested.
522: 	for _, want := range []string{"tool", "action", "title", "detail", "text", "delta"} {
523: 		if _, ok := payload[want]; ok {
524: 			continue
525: 		}
526: 		if v := findNestedString(event.Payload, want); v != "" {
527: 			payload[want] = boundedPayloadValue(v)
528: 		}
529: 	}
530: 	omission := (*runcontrol.Omission)(nil)
531: 	if event.RawPresent || event.RawOmitted {
532: 		reason := firstSafeValue(event.RawOmissionReason, "runtime payload omitted by safe persistence policy")
533: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: boundedSafe(reason), Count: 1}
534: 	} else if len(event.Payload) > len(payload)-5 {
535: 		// Payload had more fields than we persisted (truncated/omitted keys) – record for diagnostics but don't hide persisted fields.
536: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: boundedSafe("runtime payload truncated to safe observable fields"), Count: 1}
537: 	}
538: 	return runcontrol.EventDraft{
539: 		Type: eventType, Scope: runcontrol.EventScopeRuntime,
540: 		Stage: boundedSafe(req.Metadata["stage"]), Task: boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(req.Metadata["task"], req.Metadata["task.kind"])),
541: 		Kind: payload["kind"], Tool: payload["tool"], Action: payload["action"],
542: 		Reason: payload["reason"], Detail: firstSafeValue(payload["detail"], payload["title"]),
543: 		Payload: payload, Omission: omission,
544: 	}
545: }
546: 
547: func isSensitivePayloadKey(key string) bool {
548: 	lower := strings.ToLower(key)
549: 	for _, marker := range []string{"secret", "token", "password", "authorization", "cookie", "api_key", "apikey", "credential", "auth"} {
550: 		if strings.Contains(lower, marker) {
551: 			return true
552: 		}
553: 	}
554: 	return false
555: }
556: 
557: func findNestedString(payload map[string]any, want string) string {
558: 	for _, v := range payload {
559: 		if m, ok := v.(map[string]any); ok {
560: 			if s, ok := m[want].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) != "" {
561: 				return s
562: 			}
563: 			// One more level deep (common for opencode part.state structures)
564: 			for _, inner := range m {
565: 				if innerMap, ok := inner.(map[string]any); ok {
566: 					if s, ok := innerMap[want].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) != "" {
567: 						return s
568: 					}
569: 				}
570: 			}
571: 		}
572: 	}
573: 	return ""
574: }
575: 
576: func payloadValueString(value any) string {
577: 	switch v := value.(type) {
578: 	case string:
579: 		return v
580: 	case []byte:
581: 		if len(v) == 0 {
582: 			return ""
583: 		}
584: 		return string(v)
585: 	case bool:
586: 		if v {
587: 			return "true"
588: 		}
589: 		return "false"

reasoning_details.text:
Very important discovery: `controlledRuntime.StartRun` creates run-control rows with Target.Kind derived from PromptRef.OwnerKind — e.g., "sprint", "study", "runtime". These are the runtime-backed child runs (execute tasks, review workers, smoke harness invocations, QA shard runs). So the runs table contains non-"operation" target kinds.

Now the web operations DELETE fallback: `h.runs.CancelRun(r.Context(), app.RunID(id), "user_requested")` — no Target.Kind check. So DELETE /api/v1/operations/<child-run-id> where <child-run-id> is e.g. a sprint runtime child run (kind "sprint") cancels that child run, while GET /api/v1/operations/<same-id> returns 404 operation_not_found (durableOperationStatus requires Target.Kind=="operation"). Asymmetric vocabulary enforcement: status/events say "not an operation", cancel says "OK cancelled". Is this exploitable/harmful? It's an authenticated local operator action. The bad outcome: operator can cancel child runs through the wrong door with misleading semantics; also the cancel fallback doesn't verify the id looks like a run id at all (CancelRun validates format? RequestCancellation validates run ID format presumably). Severity low; it's a consistency defect in the target-check ladder the assignment explicitly names ("divergent cancellation ... target checks"). Worth reporting as low-severity inconsistency: cancel door accepts any run-control row; status/events doors filter to operation kind.

Hmm wait, actually is it even reachable? handleOperationCancel first tries hub.cancelOperation which returns errOperationNotFound when record==nil. Then falls to CancelRun. Yes reachable for any run id not in hub.

Also note handleOperationStatus: hub.status fails → durableOperationStatus requires Target.Kind=="operation" → 404 → legacyOperationID check. Consistent.

Now the bigger fish — **web-hub cancellation never persists RequestCancellation**. Let me re-verify by checking operations_test.go expectations and any place that bridges hub cancel to durable. In hub.cancelOperation → record.cancel() only. The manager control loop only reacts to CancellationRequested in DB. So hub-initiated cancel of durable op:
- DB: no cancellation_state change.
- Terminal: FinishOperation proposes cancelled reason "operation cancelled".

Observable divergences vs CLI/TUI/web-fallback cancels of the same logical operation:
1. `run show <id>` during unwind shows Cancellation: none / lifecycle running (CLI cancel shows cancelling + requested).
2. After completion, terminal reason differs ("operation cancelled" in both cases actually — FinishOperation always uses "operation cancelled"). Hmm so terminal reason same. But cancellation_state/reason columns differ: CLI path leaves cancellation_state=requested + reason user_requested permanently; web path leaves them empty. Also the durable event journal lacks the cancellation event + acknowledgement for web-initiated cancels.
3. Crash window: if server killed after DELETE but before unwind finishes, durable row remains lifecycle=running, owner dead → reconcile marks interrupted (or cleanup_uncertain via product records). Operator's cancel intent lost entirely — no cancellation request persisted. With CLI/TUI/fallback paths the intent survives as cancelling state and reconcile acknowledges it.

Is there counter-evidence? Maybe web UI's operation page uses /runs/{id} for durable state and the contract only promises terminal convergence. Let me read docs/local-web.md §cancellation and user-guide.md to see exact promised behavior. Also check tests: operations_test.go "hub lifecycle/cancellation/session ownership (:124)" — see what it asserts about durable rows on cancel.

display.text:
Loopback is not an authentication or isolation boundary against another process
running as the same OS user or a compromised local account. The local cookie is
session policy, not an account, tenant, TLS, or remote authentication model.
There is no remote-worker or LAN/public exposure. Do not proxy or port-forward
this server.

## API And Health

The bundled browser uses versioned `/api/v1` JSON resources. Success
responses use `{data, meta}`; errors use `{error, meta}` with safe stable codes.
Unknown `/api/` paths and unsupported versions always return JSON rather than an
HTML page.

This API is compatibility-controlled for the bundled browser. It is not yet a
promised public integration API and has no remote-client or pagination support.
Breaking DTO changes require an explicit version or coordinated migration.

### Guarded operation API

The command lifecycle is:

1. `POST /api/v1/operations/prepare` performs side-effect-free normalization,
   prerequisite inspection, affected-path projection, and fingerprinting.
2. The user reviews the returned scope and short-lived confirmation.
3. `POST /api/v1/operations` repeats the specification, re-normalizes it, and
   starts server-owned work only if the confirmation remains current. Success
   is `202` with a `Location` header. Retrying the same accepted session/token
   returns the original operation and Location without starting duplicate work.
4. `GET /api/v1/operations` returns the current browser session's active
   operations. The navigation uses this bounded, ephemeral collection to
   recover links to work after a page change or refresh; it never exposes
   another session's operations or treats the collection as durable state.
5. `GET /api/v1/operations/{id}` returns retained status and terminal result.
6. `GET /api/v1/operations/{id}/events` observes progress through SSE.
7. `DELETE /api/v1/operations/{id}` requests canonical cancellation and is
   idempotent.

Stable states are `accepted`, `running`, `cancelling`, `succeeded`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, `interrupted`, and `cleanup_uncertain`. Stable SSE event names are
`snapshot`, `progress`, `warning`, `finding`, `artifact`, `cancel_requested`,
`recovery_required`, and `terminal`. Event IDs are decimal and monotonic within
one operation. SSE is progress-only: disconnecting closes only that
subscription, while cancellation requires `DELETE`.

Runtime-backed progress uses an explicit safe allowlist. When supplied by the
underlying operation it may include provider and model identifiers, attempt and
runtime-attempt counts, turns, input/output/total/reasoning/cache token counts,
duration, estimated cost, and the count of retained runtime events. Preparation
shows the configured runtime/model source and duration/cost class before
confirmation. Prompt bodies, provider payloads, stderr, executable arguments,
credentials, cookies, session/CSRF values, and unsafe paths are never projected.
Prompt-version, tool-count, and fallback-selection fields are not currently
available from every shared operation and are therefore not fabricated as web
metadata; adding them requires an app-level typed field and compatibility test.

Accepted product failures remain terminal operation results returned from the
status resource with HTTP `200`. Pre-acceptance and transport errors use stable
codes including `invalid_request`, `csrf_failed`, `origin_rejected`,
`session_required`, `operation_not_found`, `confirmation_expired`,
`confirmation_mismatch`, `confirmation_replayed`, `stale_confirmation`,
`operation_conflict`, `validation_failed`, `prerequisite_unavailable`,
`operation_capacity`, `subscriber_capacity`, `server_draining`, and
`internal_failure`.

The hub is deliberately ephemeral. Durable workspace and product run state are
the recovery authority after eviction or restart. A replay gap emits
`recovery_required` plus a current snapshot; it never fabricates missing
progress. Before accepting traffic, server startup reconciles dead-owner sprint
execute/review/smoke attempts to explicit interrupted evidence while leaving
live cross-process mutation leases untouched.

### Operation bounds

| Resource | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| JSON command body | 64 KiB |
| Active operations | 8 |
| Preparations | 128 for 2 minutes |
| Retained events | 256 and 256 KiB per operation |
| Encoded event | 16 KiB |
| Terminal result | 256 KiB |
| Subscribers | 8 per operation, 32 server-wide |
| Subscriber queue | 32 events |
| Terminal retention | 10 minutes |
| Heartbeat / stream lifetime | 15 seconds / 30 minutes |

Slow subscriber queues are disconnected without blocking product work. New
work is never queued: capacity returns `429`, and draining returns `503`.

### Performance expectations

This is a single-user loopback interface, intentionally optimized for bounded
and predictable behavior rather than throughput. At the documented collection
and payload bounds on a supported developer machine, the release targets are:

| Path | Expected local behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Listener startup after validated configuration | ready within 2 seconds, excluding browser launch |
| Ordinary HTML and `/api/v1` reads | response begins within 500 ms |
| Operation preparation without external runtime work | response within 1 second |
| Initial SSE snapshot after connection | delivered within 1 second |
| Concurrent work | at most 8 active operations and 32 streams; excess work is rejected, not queued |

These are release expectations rather than hard request deadlines. CI uses
deterministic behavior, bounds, and race tests; wall-clock regressions are
confirmed on representative release hardware before publication so a loaded
shared runner does not create a misleading failure.

`GET /api/v1/health` reports only server readiness and lightweight availability
of the configured workspace query. `200`/`ok` means the server can answer that
query; `503`/`unavailable` means it cannot. Health does not validate every
artifact, scan projects or studies, contact a runtime/provider, or run review or
smoke. It is not proof that the whole product state is valid.

## Shutdown And Troubleshooting

Press Ctrl-C or send the process its normal termination signal. UltraPlan first
enters draining, rejects preparation/start, requests `server_shutdown`
cancellation exactly once for every active server-owned operation, waits up to
10 seconds for canonical product/runtime/harness cleanup and durable terminal
reconciliation, publishes terminal SSE, then stops HTTP. Deadline expiry is
reported as interrupted or cleanup-uncertain rather than success. Before the
ephemeral hub closes, the app atomically writes a product-owned
`.cleanup-uncertain.json` marker in the affected sprint. Startup reconciles the
marker under the normal sprint mutation lease; if no canonical running record
can be reconciled, the marker remains available for inspection. Server startup
fails closed until that uncertainty is resolved, rather than accepting
new sprint mutations over ambiguous state. Browser disconnect never triggers
this sequence.

Key doc statements:

- local-web.md:139-142: "GET /api/v1/operations returns the current browser session's active operations... it never exposes another session's operations or treats the collection as durable state." — the ACTIVE list is session-scoped by contract. But `handleActiveOperations` merges durable run-control rows (TargetKind=operation, any owner, any session) into the response! Wait — re-read: "returns the current browser session's active operations. The navigation uses this bounded, ephemeral collection to recover links to work after a page change or refresh; it never exposes another session's operations". Hmm — but the merge adds durable operations from ALL sessions and CLI. Is that "another session's operations"? Yes literally: browser session B's durable-backed ops appear in A's list (hub record belongs to B's session, but the runs page query is global). Also CLI-created operation runs appear.

Hold on — is that a defect per contract? The contract says the endpoint "never exposes another session's operations". The implementation appends durableActiveOperation(snapshot) for every active operation-kind run in the workspace regardless of which session/door started it. So browser A sees B's operations AND their IDs, and can then GET /api/v1/operations/{id} (durable fallback has no session check → full status) and DELETE them (fallback CancelRun → cancels!). That directly contradicts local-web.md:142 "never exposes another session's operations".

Hmm wait, but maybe the intent is: hub records are session-scoped; the durable merge exists so that after server restart... no wait, after restart the hub is empty but runs are still listed. Actually why does handleActiveOperations query runs at all? To show operations owned by OTHER processes (CLI/TUI)? The comment in context pack says "active-operations list merges hub records with a run-control page of TargetKind=operation lifecycles accepted/queued/running/cancelling". If the contract says the collection must never expose another session's operations, then merging cross-session durable rows violates it. Unless "another session's operations" refers only to hub-ephemeral ones ("treats the collection as durable state" — i.e., the collection itself is ephemeral). Ambiguous drafting. Let me look at the test for active operations to see what behavior is pinned. Search operations_test.go for active.

Also user-guide.md:379-390: "cancellation state ... shown [on every surface]"; "a cancellation request can lose the race..." — read exact lines 370-395.

Let me also check the web UI static JS to see whether it calls GET /api/v1/operations for nav recovery only.

But first — the more clear-cut finding remains: hub cancel doesn't persist cancellation into run-control. Doc evidence: user-guide.md:385 "a cancellation request can lose the race..." let me read that passage fully.

the skill performs the selected stage and reconciles status afterward.

For area and final reasoning, an explicit deep-dive request should become an
interactive design discussion covering evidence, alternatives, trade-offs,
risks, technical debt, and future consequences before conclusions are written.
See [Manually Invoked Stage Skills](stage-skills.md) for the complete contract.
## Watching and controlling durable runs

Every runtime-backed CLI command, confirmed web/TUI operation, and external
smoke execution receives a durable run before work starts. Use `ultraplan run
list` or the web/TUI Runs view to find it. The same ID, lifecycle, liveness,
cancellation state, product status, retention state, and event cursor are shown
on every surface.

Lifecycle answers what the operation has durably decided; liveness answers
whether its current owner is known to be running. Product status is separate.
For example, `running / stalled / product unknown` is meaningful and must not
be displayed as success. Likewise, a cancellation request can lose the
immutable terminal race to a completion that had already committed.

Use `run follow` for observation and `run cancel` for control. Closing a tab,
leaving a TUI view, quitting the TUI, or interrupting `run follow` does not
cancel work. A compacted or tombstone record remains truthful about its current
snapshot even when full event history is no longer available.

## Reading QA evidence

Run `qa --dry-run` to inspect the current map without state writes. A normal
start retains frozen plans and evidence from disposable copies, then publishes
adjudication, promoted issue summaries, regression candidates, a canonical
assessment, and `qa.md`. Evidence can be accepted, rejected, or blocked;
rejected and incomplete evidence never disappears into a passing assessment.
QA does not apply generated changes, repair production code, weaken governed
expectations, mutate Git, or change the independent Conformance Review verdict.

Use `qa --suite smoke` when the next QA action is the canonical containing
smoke suite. It produces the same external harness run and `smoke.md` authority
as the `smoke` command. A narrow or diagnostic smoke run cannot substitute for
that evidence. Inspect status after cancellation or failure. Resume only a
current normal QA attempt; smoke-suite retries are new starts.

Contract (user-guide.md:374-380): "The same ID, lifecycle, liveness, **cancellation state**, product status, retention state, and event cursor are shown on every surface."

So the contract explicitly says cancellation state is shown identically on every surface. When a browser cancels a durable operation through DELETE /api/v1/operations/{id}:
- The operations API shows state "cancelling" (hub in-memory).

136: func (r *SQLiteRepository) AcknowledgeCancellation(ctx context.Context, fence Fence) (Snapshot, bool, error) {
137: 	if ctx == nil {
138: 		ctx = context.Background()
139: 	}
140: 	if err := fence.Validate(); err != nil {
141: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
142: 	}
143: 	now := r.now()
144: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
145: 	if err != nil {
146: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_begin", "begin cancellation acknowledgement failed", err)
147: 	}
148: 	defer tx.Rollback()
149: 	if err := verifyFence(ctx, tx, fence); err != nil {
150: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
151: 	}
152: 	current, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, fence.RunID)
153: 	if err != nil {
154: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
155: 	}
156: 	if current.Terminal != nil || current.Cancellation.State == CancellationAcknowledged {
157: 		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
158: 			return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_read_commit", "finish cancellation acknowledgement read failed", err)
159: 		}
160: 		return current, false, nil
161: 	}
162: 	if current.Cancellation.State != CancellationRequested {
163: 		return Snapshot{}, false, runError(CodeConflict, "cancel_ack", fence.RunID, "cancellation has not been requested", false, nil)
164: 	}
165: 	sequence := current.LastSequence + 1
166: 	payload, _ := marshalBounded(map[string]string{"state": string(CancellationAcknowledged)}, MaxSafeValueBytes)
167: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO events (run_id, sequence, committed_at, event_type, attempt_id, payload_json)
168: VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'cancellation', ?, ?)`, string(fence.RunID), sequence, formatTime(now), string(fence.AttemptID), payload); err != nil {
169: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_event", "persist cancellation acknowledgement event failed", err)
170: 	}
171: 	result, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `
172: UPDATE runs SET cancellation_state = ?, cancellation_acknowledged_at = ?, updated_at = ?, last_sequence = ?
173: WHERE run_id = ? AND current_attempt_id = ? AND cancellation_state = ? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL AND last_sequence = ?`,
174: 		string(CancellationAcknowledged), formatTime(now), formatTime(now), sequence, string(fence.RunID), string(fence.AttemptID),
175: 		string(CancellationRequested), current.LastSequence)
176: 	if err != nil {
177: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack", "persist cancellation acknowledgement failed", err)
178: 	}
179: 	if changed, err := result.RowsAffected(); err != nil || changed != 1 {
180: 		return Snapshot{}, false, runError(CodeStaleFence, "cancel_ack", fence.RunID, "cancellation acknowledgement lost its fence", false, err)
181: 	}
182: 	snapshot, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, fence.RunID)
183: 	if err != nil {
184: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
185: 	}
186: 	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
187: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_commit", "commit cancellation acknowledgement failed", err)
188: 	}
189: 	r.notify(fence.RunID, sequence)
190: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "run cancellation acknowledged",
191: 		LogField{Key: "run_id", Value: string(fence.RunID)}, LogField{Key: "attempt_id", Value: string(fence.AttemptID)},
192: 		LogField{Key: "sequence", Value: fmt.Sprint(sequence)}, LogField{Key: "cancellation_state", Value: string(snapshot.Cancellation.State)})
193: 	return snapshot, true, nil

301: func (r *SQLiteRepository) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, probe ProcessProbe, opts ReconcileOptions) (ReconcileReport, error) {
302: 	if probe == nil {
303: 		return ReconcileReport{}, invalidField("process_probe", "is required")
304: 	}
305: 	grace := opts.Grace
306: 	if grace == 0 {
307: 		grace = ReconciliationGrace
308: 	}
309: 	if grace < 0 {
310: 		return ReconcileReport{}, invalidField("reconciliation.grace", "must not be negative")
311: 	}
312: 	limit := opts.Limit
313: 	if limit == 0 {
314: 		limit = DefaultReconcileBatch
315: 	}
316: 	if limit < 1 || limit > MaximumReconcileBatch {
317: 		return ReconcileReport{}, invalidField("reconciliation.limit", fmt.Sprintf("must be between 1 and %d", MaximumReconcileBatch))
318: 	}
319: 	report := ReconcileReport{Decisions: make([]ReconcileDecision, 0, limit)}
320: 	acceptedPredicate, acceptedArgs := r.expiredTimestampPredicate("accepted_at", grace)
321: 	unclaimedRows, err := r.db.QueryContext(ctx, `
322: SELECT run_id FROM runs
323: WHERE terminal_outcome IS NULL AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND `+acceptedPredicate+`
324: ORDER BY accepted_at ASC, run_id ASC LIMIT ?`, append(acceptedArgs, limit)...)
325: 	if err != nil {
326: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "scan unclaimed runs failed", err)
327: 	}
328: 	var unclaimed []RunID
329: 	for unclaimedRows.Next() {
330: 		var runID RunID
331: 		if err := unclaimedRows.Scan(&runID); err != nil {
332: 			unclaimedRows.Close()
333: 			return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "decode unclaimed run failed", err)
334: 		}
335: 		unclaimed = append(unclaimed, runID)
336: 	}
337: 	if err := unclaimedRows.Close(); err != nil {
338: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "close unclaimed run scan failed", err)
339: 	}
340: 	for _, runID := range unclaimed {
341: 		won, err := r.reconcileUnclaimed(ctx, runID)
342: 		if err != nil {
343: 			return report, err
344: 		}
345: 		if !won {
346: 			continue
347: 		}
348: 		report.Scanned++
349: 		report.Terminal++
350: 		decision := "owner_never_claimed_after_grace"
351: 		candidate := reconciliationCandidate{runID: runID}
352: 		_ = r.recordReconciliation(ctx, candidate, "terminal_proposal", decision)
353: 		report.Decisions = append(report.Decisions, ReconcileDecision{RunID: runID, Action: "terminal_proposal", Decision: decision})
354: 	}
355: 	remaining := limit - report.Scanned
356: 	if remaining == 0 {
357: 		r.finishReconciliationLog(ctx, &report)
358: 		return report, nil
359: 	}
360: 	predicate, predicateArgs := r.expiredLeasePredicate(grace)
361: 	queryArgs := append(predicateArgs, remaining)
362: 	rows, err := r.db.QueryContext(ctx, `
363: SELECT runs.run_id, attempts.attempt_id, attempts.owner_id, attempts.fencing_generation,
364:        attempts.host_digest, attempts.boot_id, attempts.pid, attempts.process_birth_token
365: FROM runs JOIN attempts ON attempts.attempt_id = runs.current_attempt_id
366: WHERE runs.terminal_outcome IS NULL AND `+predicate+`
367: ORDER BY attempts.lease_expires_at ASC, runs.run_id ASC LIMIT ?`, queryArgs...)
368: 	if err != nil {
369: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "scan expired run owners failed", err)
370: 	}
371: 	var candidates []reconciliationCandidate
372: 	for rows.Next() {
373: 		var candidate reconciliationCandidate
374: 		if err := rows.Scan(&candidate.runID, &candidate.attemptID, &candidate.ownerID, &candidate.generation,
375: 			&candidate.process.HostDigest, &candidate.process.BootID, &candidate.process.PID, &candidate.process.BirthToken); err != nil {
376: 			rows.Close()
377: 			return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "decode expired run owner failed", err)
378: 		}
379: 		candidates = append(candidates, candidate)
380: 	}
381: 	if err := rows.Close(); err != nil {
382: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "close expired owner scan failed", err)
383: 	}
384: 	report.Scanned += len(candidates)
385: 	for _, candidate := range candidates {
386: 		observed, probeErr := probe.Probe(ctx, candidate.process.PID)
387: 		decision, outcome := reconcileProcessDecision(candidate.process, observed, probeErr)
388: 		action := "terminal_proposal"
389: 		if outcome == "" {
390: 			action = "mark_stalled"
391: 			if err := r.markStalled(ctx, candidate); err != nil {
392: 				if errors.Is(err, ErrTerminal) || errors.Is(err, ErrStaleFence) {
393: 					continue
394: 				}
395: 				return report, err
396: 			}
397: 			report.Stalled++
398: 		} else {
399: 			fence := Fence{RunID: candidate.runID, AttemptID: candidate.attemptID, OwnerID: candidate.ownerID, FencingGeneration: candidate.generation}
400: 			_, won, err := r.ProposeTerminal(ctx, fence, TerminalProposal{Outcome: outcome, Reason: decision, ProposedBy: "reconciler"})
401: 			if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, ErrTerminal) && !errors.Is(err, ErrStaleFence) {
402: 				return report, err
403: 			}
404: 			if won {
405: 				report.Terminal++
406: 				if outcome == TerminalCleanupUncertain {
407: 					report.Uncertain++
408: 				}
409: 			}
410: 		}
411: 		_ = r.recordReconciliation(ctx, candidate, action, decision)
412: 		report.Decisions = append(report.Decisions, ReconcileDecision{RunID: candidate.runID, AttemptID: candidate.attemptID, Action: action, Decision: decision})
413: 	}
414: 	r.finishReconciliationLog(ctx, &report)
415: 	return report, nil
416: }

428: 	metricStarted := time.Now()
429: 	defer func() { r.metrics.terminal.observe(metricStarted, resultErr) }()

431: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
432: 	if err != nil {
433: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_begin", "begin unclaimed reconciliation failed", err)
434: 	}

438: 		if errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) {
439: 			return false, nil
440: 		}

442: 	}

445: 	}

447: 	reason := "owner_never_claimed_after_grace"
448: 	payload, err := marshalBounded(map[string]string{"outcome": string(TerminalInterrupted), "reason": reason}, MaxSafeValueBytes*2)

450: 		return false, err

452: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO events (run_id, sequence, committed_at, event_type, payload_json)
453: VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'terminal', ?)`, string(runID), sequence, formatTime(now), payload); err != nil {
454: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_event", "persist unclaimed terminal event failed", err)
455: 	}
456: 	result, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `UPDATE runs SET lifecycle = ?, liveness = ?, finished_at = ?, updated_at = ?, last_sequence = ?,
457: terminal_outcome = ?, terminal_reason = ?, terminal_at = ?, terminal_proposed_by = 'reconciler'
458: WHERE run_id = ? AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`,
459: 		string(LifecycleInterrupted), string(LivenessTerminal), formatTime(now), formatTime(now), sequence,
460: 		string(TerminalInterrupted), reason, formatTime(now), string(runID))

462: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_cas", "persist unclaimed terminal state failed", err)

466: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_cas", "inspect unclaimed terminal state failed", err)
467: 	}
468: 	if changed != 1 {
469: 		return false, nil
470: 	}
471: 	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {

475: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "unclaimed run reconciled",
476: 		LogField{Key: "run_id", Value: string(runID)}, LogField{Key: "sequence", Value: fmt.Sprint(sequence)},
477: 		LogField{Key: "terminal_outcome", Value: string(TerminalInterrupted)})

481: func reconcileProcessDecision(expected, observed ProcessIdentity, probeErr error) (string, TerminalOutcome) {
482: 	if errors.Is(probeErr, ErrProcessNotFound) {
483: 		return "owner_process_missing_after_grace", TerminalInterrupted
484: 	}
485: 	if probeErr != nil {
486: 		return "owner_process_identity_uncertain_after_grace", TerminalCleanupUncertain
487: 	}

489: 		return "owner_process_identity_incomplete_after_grace", TerminalCleanupUncertain
490: 	}
491: 	if expected.HostDigest != observed.HostDigest || expected.BootID != observed.BootID || expected.PID != observed.PID || expected.BirthToken != observed.BirthToken {
492: 		return "owner_process_birth_mismatch_after_grace", TerminalInterrupted
493: 	}
494: 	return "exact_owner_process_still_live_but_lease_expired", ""
495: }

37: 	}
38: 	result, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `
39: UPDATE attempts SET heartbeat_at = ?, lease_expires_at = ?
40: WHERE run_id = ? AND attempt_id = ? AND owner_id = ? AND fencing_generation = ? AND outcome IS NULL`,
41: 		formatTime(now), formatTime(now.Add(lease)), string(fence.RunID), string(fence.AttemptID), fence.OwnerID, fence.FencingGeneration)
42: 	if err != nil {
43: 		return Snapshot{}, classifyStoreError("heartbeat", "persist owner heartbeat failed", err)
44: 	}
45: 	if changed, err := result.RowsAffected(); err != nil || changed != 1 {
46: 		return Snapshot{}, runError(CodeStaleFence, "heartbeat", fence.RunID, "owner heartbeat lost its authoritative fence", false, err)
47: 	}
48: 	result, err = tx.ExecContext(ctx, `UPDATE runs SET liveness = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE run_id = ? AND current_attempt_id = ? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`,
49: 		string(LivenessLive), formatTime(now), string(fence.RunID), string(fence.AttemptID))
50: 	if err != nil {
51: 		return Snapshot{}, classifyStoreError("heartbeat_snapshot", "update heartbeat snapshot failed", err)
52: 	}
53: 	if changed, err := result.RowsAffected(); err != nil || changed != 1 {
54: 		return Snapshot{}, runError(CodeStaleFence, "heartbeat", fence.RunID, "run is no longer owned by heartbeat attempt", false, err)
55: 	}
56: 	snapshot, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, fence.RunID)
57: 	if err != nil {
58: 		return Snapshot{}, err
59: 	}
60: 	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
61: 		return Snapshot{}, classifyStoreError("heartbeat_commit", "commit owner heartbeat failed", err)
62: 	}
63: 	r.log(ctx, LogDebug, "run owner heartbeat committed",
64: 		LogField{Key: "run_id", Value: string(fence.RunID)}, LogField{Key: "attempt_id", Value: string(fence.AttemptID)},
65: 		LogField{Key: "owner_id", Value: fence.OwnerID}, LogField{Key: "fencing_generation", Value: fmt.Sprint(fence.FencingGeneration)})
66: 	r.metrics.leaseRenewals.Add(1)
67: 	return snapshot, nil
68: }

70: func (r *SQLiteRepository) RequestCancellation(ctx context.Context, runID RunID, reason string) (Snapshot, bool, error) {
71: 	if ctx == nil {
72: 		ctx = context.Background()
73: 	}
74: 	if err := runID.Validate(); err != nil {
75: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
76: 	}
77: 	reason = strings.TrimSpace(reason)
78: 	if reason == "" || len(reason) > MaxSafeValueBytes || strings.ContainsAny(reason, "\x00\r\n") {
79: 		return Snapshot{}, false, invalidField("cancellation.reason", "must be a bounded canonical reason")
80: 	}
81: 	now := r.now()
82: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
83: 	if err != nil {
84: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_begin", "begin cancellation request failed", err)
85: 	}
86: 	defer tx.Rollback()
87: 	current, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, runID)
88: 	if err != nil {
89: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
90: 	}
91: 	if current.Terminal != nil || current.Cancellation.State != CancellationNone {
92: 		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
93: 			return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_read_commit", "finish cancellation state read failed", err)
94: 		}
95: 		return current, false, nil
96: 	}
97: 	sequence := current.LastSequence + 1
98: 	payload, err := marshalBounded(map[string]string{"state": string(CancellationRequested), "reason": reason}, MaxSafeValueBytes*2)
99: 	if err != nil {
100: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
101: 	}
102: 	var attemptValue any
103: 	if current.CurrentAttemptID != "" {
104: 		attemptValue = string(current.CurrentAttemptID)
105: 	}
106: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO events (run_id, sequence, committed_at, event_type, attempt_id, payload_json)
107: VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'cancellation', ?, ?)`, string(runID), sequence, formatTime(now), attemptValue, payload); err != nil {
108: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_event", "persist cancellation event failed", err)
109: 	}
110: 	result, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `
111: UPDATE runs SET lifecycle = ?, cancellation_state = ?, cancellation_reason = ?, cancellation_requested_at = ?, updated_at = ?, last_sequence = ?
112: WHERE run_id = ? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL AND cancellation_state = ? AND last_sequence = ?`,
113: 		string(LifecycleCancelling), string(CancellationRequested), reason, formatTime(now), formatTime(now), sequence,
114: 		string(runID), string(CancellationNone), current.LastSequence)
115: 	if err != nil {
116: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel", "persist cancellation request failed", err)
117: 	}
118: 	if changed, err := result.RowsAffected(); err != nil || changed != 1 {
119: 		return Snapshot{}, false, runError(CodeConflict, "cancel", runID, "cancellation state changed concurrently", true, err)
120: 	}
121: 	snapshot, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, runID)
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
124: 	}
125: 	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
126: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_commit", "commit cancellation request failed", err)
127: 	}
128: 	r.notify(runID, sequence)
129: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "run cancellation requested",
130: 		LogField{Key: "run_id", Value: string(runID)}, LogField{Key: "sequence", Value: fmt.Sprint(sequence)},
131: 		LogField{Key: "cancellation_state", Value: string(snapshot.Cancellation.State)}, LogField{Key: "cancellation_reason", Value: reason})
132: 	r.metrics.cancellationRequests.Add(1)
133: 	return snapshot, true, nil
134: }

136: func (r *SQLiteRepository) AcknowledgeCancellation(ctx context.Context, fence Fence) (Snapshot, bool, error) {
137: 	if ctx == nil {
138: 		ctx = context.Background()
139: 	}
140: 	if err := fence.Validate(); err != nil {
141: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
142: 	}
143: 	now := r.now()
144: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
145: 	if err != nil {
146: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_begin", "begin cancellation acknowledgement failed", err)
147: 	}
148: 	defer tx.Rollback()
149: 	if err := verifyFence(ctx, tx, fence); err != nil {
150: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
151: 	}
152: 	current, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, fence.RunID)
153: 	if err != nil {
154: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
155: 	}
156: 	if current.Terminal != nil || current.Cancellation.State == CancellationAcknowledged {
157: 		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
158: 			return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_read_commit", "finish cancellation acknowledgement read failed", err)
159: 		}
160: 		return current, false, nil
161: 	}
162: 	if current.Cancellation.State != CancellationRequested {
163: 		return Snapshot{}, false, runError(CodeConflict, "cancel_ack", fence.RunID, "cancellation has not been requested", false, nil)
164: 	}
165: 	sequence := current.LastSequence + 1
166: 	payload, _ := marshalBounded(map[string]string{"state": string(CancellationAcknowledged)}, MaxSafeValueBytes)
167: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO events (run_id, sequence, committed_at, event_type, attempt_id, payload_json)
168: VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'cancellation', ?, ?)`, string(fence.RunID), sequence, formatTime(now), string(fence.AttemptID), payload); err != nil {
169: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_event", "persist cancellation acknowledgement event failed", err)
170: 	}
171: 	result, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `
172: UPDATE runs SET cancellation_state = ?, cancellation_acknowledged_at = ?, updated_at = ?, last_sequence = ?
173: WHERE run_id = ? AND current_attempt_id = ? AND cancellation_state = ? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL AND last_sequence = ?`,
174: 		string(CancellationAcknowledged), formatTime(now), formatTime(now), sequence, string(fence.RunID), string(fence.AttemptID),
175: 		string(CancellationRequested), current.LastSequence)
176: 	if err != nil {
177: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack", "persist cancellation acknowledgement failed", err)
178: 	}
179: 	if changed, err := result.RowsAffected(); err != nil || changed != 1 {
180: 		return Snapshot{}, false, runError(CodeStaleFence, "cancel_ack", fence.RunID, "cancellation acknowledgement lost its fence", false, err)
181: 	}
182: 	snapshot, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, fence.RunID)
183: 	if err != nil {
184: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
185: 	}
186: 	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
187: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_commit", "commit cancellation acknowledgement failed", err)
188: 	}
189: 	r.notify(fence.RunID, sequence)
190: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "run cancellation acknowledged",
191: 		LogField{Key: "run_id", Value: string(fence.RunID)}, LogField{Key: "attempt_id", Value: string(fence.AttemptID)},
192: 		LogField{Key: "sequence", Value: fmt.Sprint(sequence)}, LogField{Key: "cancellation_state", Value: string(snapshot.Cancellation.State)})
193: 	return snapshot, true, nil
194: }

196: func (r *SQLiteRepository) List(ctx context.Context, query Query) (Page, error) {
197: 	limit := query.Limit
198: 	if limit == 0 {
199: 		limit = 50
200: 	}
201: 	if limit < 1 || limit > 200 {
202: 		return Page{}, invalidField("query.limit", "must be between 1 and 200")
203: 	}
204: 	clauses := []string{"1=1"}
205: 	args := make([]any, 0, 8)
206: 	if len(query.Lifecycle) > 0 {
207: 		parts := make([]string, 0, len(query.Lifecycle))
208: 		for _, lifecycle := range query.Lifecycle {
209: 			if !lifecycle.IsValid() {
210: 				return Page{}, invalidField("query.lifecycle", "contains an unknown state")
211: 			}
212: 			parts = append(parts, "?")
213: 			args = append(args, string(lifecycle))
214: 		}
215: 		clauses = append(clauses, "lifecycle IN ("+strings.Join(parts, ",")+")")
216: 	}
217: 	for column, value := range map[string]string{
218: 		"target_kind": query.TargetKind, "project_id": query.Project, "sprint_id": query.Sprint, "study_id": query.Study,
219: 	} {
220: 		if value != "" {
221: 			clauses = append(clauses, column+" = ?")
222: 			args = append(args, value)
223: 		}
224: 	}
225: 	if query.After != "" {
226: 		cursor, err := decodeRunCursor(query.After)
227: 		if err != nil {
228: 			return Page{}, err
229: 		}
230: 		clauses = append(clauses, "(updated_at < ? OR (updated_at = ? AND run_id < ?))")
231: 		args = append(args, cursor.UpdatedAt, cursor.UpdatedAt, string(cursor.RunID))
232: 	}
233: 	rows, err := r.db.QueryContext(ctx, `SELECT run_id, updated_at FROM runs WHERE `+strings.Join(clauses, " AND ")+` ORDER BY updated_at DESC, run_id DESC LIMIT ?`, append(args, limit+1)...)
234: 	if err != nil {
235: 		return Page{}, classifyStoreError("list", "list runs failed", err)
236: 	}
237: 	defer rows.Close()
238: 	type listedRun struct {
239: 		id        RunID
240: 		updatedAt string
241: 	}
242: 	listed := make([]listedRun, 0, limit+1)
243: 	for rows.Next() {
244: 		var item listedRun
245: 		if err := rows.Scan(&item.id, &item.updatedAt); err != nil {
246: 			return Page{}, classifyStoreError("list_scan", "decode run list failed", err)
247: 		}
248: 		listed = append(listed, item)
249: 	}
250: 	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
251: 		return Page{}, classifyStoreError("list_rows", "read run list failed", err)
252: 	}
253: 	page := Page{Runs: make([]Snapshot, 0, min(limit, len(listed)))}
254: 	if len(listed) > limit {
255: 		page.NextCursor = encodeRunCursor(runCursor{UpdatedAt: listed[limit-1].updatedAt, RunID: listed[limit-1].id})
256: 		listed = listed[:limit]
257: 	}
258: 	for _, item := range listed {
259: 		snapshot, err := r.Snapshot(ctx, item.id)
260: 		if err != nil {
261: 			return Page{}, err
262: 		}
263: 		page.Runs = append(page.Runs, snapshot)
264: 	}
265: 	return page, nil
266: }

268: type runCursor struct {
269: 	UpdatedAt string `json:"updated_at"`
270: 	RunID     RunID  `json:"run_id"`
271: }
272: 
273: func encodeRunCursor(cursor runCursor) string {
274: 	encoded, _ := json.Marshal(cursor)
275: 	return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(encoded)
276: }
277: 
278: func decodeRunCursor(value string) (runCursor, error) {
279: 	encoded, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(value)
280: 	if err != nil || len(encoded) > 1024 {
281: 		return runCursor{}, invalidField("query.after", "is not a valid opaque cursor")
282: 	}
283: 	var cursor runCursor
284: 	if err := json.Unmarshal(encoded, &cursor); err != nil || cursor.UpdatedAt == "" || cursor.RunID.Validate() != nil {
285: 		return runCursor{}, invalidField("query.after", "is not a valid opaque cursor")
286: 	}
287: 	if _, err := parseTime(cursor.UpdatedAt); err != nil {
288: 		return runCursor{}, invalidField("query.after", "is not a valid opaque cursor")
289: 	}
290: 	return cursor, nil
291: }

293: type reconciliationCandidate struct {
294: 	runID      RunID
295: 	attemptID  AttemptID
296: 	ownerID    string
297: 	generation uint64
298: 	process    ProcessIdentity
299: }

301: func (r *SQLiteRepository) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, probe ProcessProbe, opts ReconcileOptions) (ReconcileReport, error) {
302: 	if probe == nil {
303: 		return ReconcileReport{}, invalidField("process_probe", "is required")
304: 	}
305: 	grace := opts.Grace
306: 	if grace == 0 {
307: 		grace = ReconciliationGrace
308: 	}
309: 	if grace < 0 {
310: 		return ReconcileReport{}, invalidField("reconciliation.grace", "must not be negative")
311: 	}
312: 	limit := opts.Limit
313: 	if limit == 0 {
314: 		limit = DefaultReconcileBatch
315: 	}
316: 	if limit < 1 || limit > MaximumReconcileBatch {
317: 		return ReconcileReport{}, invalidField("reconciliation.limit", fmt.Sprintf("must be between 1 and %d", MaximumReconcileBatch))
318: 	}
319: 	report := ReconcileReport{Decisions: make([]ReconcileDecision, 0, limit)}
320: 	acceptedPredicate, acceptedArgs := r.expiredTimestampPredicate("accepted_at", grace)
321: 	unclaimedRows, err := r.db.QueryContext(ctx, `
322: SELECT run_id FROM runs
323: WHERE terminal_outcome IS NULL AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND `+acceptedPredicate+`
324: ORDER BY accepted_at ASC, run_id ASC LIMIT ?`, append(acceptedArgs, limit)...)
325: 	if err != nil {
326: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "scan unclaimed runs failed", err)
327: 	}
328: 	var unclaimed []RunID
329: 	for unclaimedRows.Next() {
330: 		var runID RunID
331: 		if err := unclaimedRows.Scan(&runID); err != nil {
332: 			unclaimedRows.Close()
333: 			return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "decode unclaimed run failed", err)
334: 		}
335: 		unclaimed = append(unclaimed, runID)
336: 	}
337: 	if err := unclaimedRows.Close(); err != nil {
338: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "close unclaimed run scan failed", err)
339: 	}
340: 	for _, runID := range unclaimed {
341: 		won, err := r.reconcileUnclaimed(ctx, runID)
342: 		if err != nil {
343: 			return report, err
344: 		}
345: 		if !won {
346: 			continue
347: 		}
348: 		report.Scanned++
349: 		report.Terminal++
350: 		decision := "owner_never_claimed_after_grace"
351: 		candidate := reconciliationCandidate{runID: runID}
352: 		_ = r.recordReconciliation(ctx, candidate, "terminal_proposal", decision)
353: 		report.Decisions = append(report.Decisions, ReconcileDecision{RunID: runID, Action: "terminal_proposal", Decision: decision})
354: 	}
355: 	remaining := limit - report.Scanned
356: 	if remaining == 0 {
357: 		r.finishReconciliationLog(ctx, &report)
358: 		return report, nil
359: 	}
360: 	predicate, predicateArgs := r.expiredLeasePredicate(grace)
361: 	queryArgs := append(predicateArgs, remaining)
362: 	rows, err := r.db.QueryContext(ctx, `
363: SELECT runs.run_id, attempts.attempt_id, attempts.owner_id, attempts.fencing_generation,
364:        attempts.host_digest, attempts.boot_id, attempts.pid, attempts.process_birth_token
365: FROM runs JOIN attempts ON attempts.attempt_id = runs.current_attempt_id
366: WHERE runs.terminal_outcome IS NULL AND `+predicate+`
367: ORDER BY attempts.lease_expires_at ASC, runs.run_id ASC LIMIT ?`, queryArgs...)
368: 	if err != nil {
369: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "scan expired run owners failed", err)
370: 	}
371: 	var candidates []reconciliationCandidate
372: 	for rows.Next() {
373: 		var candidate reconciliationCandidate
374: 		if err := rows.Scan(&candidate.runID, &candidate.attemptID, &candidate.ownerID, &candidate.generation,
375: 			&candidate.process.HostDigest, &candidate.process.BootID, &candidate.process.PID, &candidate.process.BirthToken); err != nil {
376: 			rows.Close()
377: 			return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "decode expired run owner failed", err)
378: 		}
379: 		candidates = append(candidates, candidate)
380: 	}
381: 	if err := rows.Close(); err != nil {
382: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "close expired owner scan failed", err)
383: 	}
384: 	report.Scanned += len(candidates)
385: 	for _, candidate := range candidates {
386: 		observed, probeErr := probe.Probe(ctx, candidate.process.PID)
387: 		decision, outcome := reconcileProcessDecision(candidate.process, observed, probeErr)
388: 		action := "terminal_proposal"
389: 		if outcome == "" {
390: 			action = "mark_stalled"
391: 			if err := r.markStalled(ctx, candidate); err != nil {
392: 				if errors.Is(err, ErrTerminal) || errors.Is(err, ErrStaleFence) {
393: 					continue
394: 				}
395: 				return report, err
396: 			}
397: 			report.Stalled++
398: 		} else {
399: 			fence := Fence{RunID: candidate.runID, AttemptID: candidate.attemptID, OwnerID: candidate.ownerID, FencingGeneration: candidate.generation}
400: 			_, won, err := r.ProposeTerminal(ctx, fence, TerminalProposal{Outcome: outcome, Reason: decision, ProposedBy: "reconciler"})
401: 			if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, ErrTerminal) && !errors.Is(err, ErrStaleFence) {
402: 				return report, err
403: 			}
404: 			if won {
405: 				report.Terminal++
406: 				if outcome == TerminalCleanupUncertain {
407: 					report.Uncertain++
408: 				}
409: 			}
410: 		}
411: 		_ = r.recordReconciliation(ctx, candidate, action, decision)
412: 		report.Decisions = append(report.Decisions, ReconcileDecision{RunID: candidate.runID, AttemptID: candidate.attemptID, Action: action, Decision: decision})
413: 	}
414: 	r.finishReconciliationLog(ctx, &report)
415: 	return report, nil
416: }

418: func (r *SQLiteRepository) finishReconciliationLog(ctx context.Context, report *ReconcileReport) {
419: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "run reconciliation completed",
420: 		LogField{Key: "reconciliation_scanned", Value: fmt.Sprint(report.Scanned)},
421: 		LogField{Key: "reconciliation_stalled", Value: fmt.Sprint(report.Stalled)},
422: 		LogField{Key: "reconciliation_terminal", Value: fmt.Sprint(report.Terminal)},
423: 		LogField{Key: "reconciliation_uncertain", Value: fmt.Sprint(report.Uncertain)})
424: 	r.metrics.reconciliations.Add(1)
425: }

427: func (r *SQLiteRepository) reconcileUnclaimed(ctx context.Context, runID RunID) (wonResult bool, resultErr error) {
428: 	metricStarted := time.Now()
429: 	defer func() { r.metrics.terminal.observe(metricStarted, resultErr) }()
430: 	now := r.now()
431: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
432: 	if err != nil {
433: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_begin", "begin unclaimed reconciliation failed", err)
434: 	}
435: 	defer tx.Rollback()
436: 	current, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, runID)
437: 	if err != nil {
438: 		if errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) {
439: 			return false, nil
440: 		}
441: 		return false, err
442: 	}
443: 	if current.Terminal != nil || current.CurrentAttemptID != "" {
444: 		return false, nil
445: 	}
446: 	sequence := current.LastSequence + 1
447: 	reason := "owner_never_claimed_after_grace"
448: 	payload, err := marshalBounded(map[string]string{"outcome": string(TerminalInterrupted), "reason": reason}, MaxSafeValueBytes*2)
449: 	if err != nil {
450: 		return false, err
451: 	}
452: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO events (run_id, sequence, committed_at, event_type, payload_json)
453: VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'terminal', ?)`, string(runID), sequence, formatTime(now), payload); err != nil {
454: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_event", "persist unclaimed terminal event failed", err)
455: 	}
456: 	result, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `UPDATE runs SET lifecycle = ?, liveness = ?, finished_at = ?, updated_at = ?, last_sequence = ?,
457: terminal_outcome = ?, terminal_reason = ?, terminal_at = ?, terminal_proposed_by = 'reconciler'
458: WHERE run_id = ? AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`,
459: 		string(LifecycleInterrupted), string(LivenessTerminal), formatTime(now), formatTime(now), sequence,
460: 		string(TerminalInterrupted), reason, formatTime(now), string(runID))
461: 	if err != nil {
462: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_cas", "persist unclaimed terminal state failed", err)
463: 	}
464: 	changed, err := result.RowsAffected()
465: 	if err != nil {
466: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_cas", "inspect unclaimed terminal state failed", err)
467: 	}
468: 	if changed != 1 {
469: 		return false, nil
470: 	}
471: 	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
472: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_commit", "commit unclaimed reconciliation failed", err)
473: 	}
474: 	r.notify(runID, sequence)
475: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "unclaimed run reconciled",
476: 		LogField{Key: "run_id", Value: string(runID)}, LogField{Key: "sequence", Value: fmt.Sprint(sequence)},
477: 		LogField{Key: "terminal_outcome", Value: string(TerminalInterrupted)})
478: 	return true, nil
479: }
480: 
481: func reconcileProcessDecision(expected, observed ProcessIdentity, probeErr error) (string, TerminalOutcome) {
482: 	if errors.Is(probeErr, ErrProcessNotFound) {
483: 		return "owner_process_missing_after_grace", TerminalInterrupted
484: 	}
485: 	if probeErr != nil {
486: 		return "owner_process_identity_uncertain_after_grace", TerminalCleanupUncertain
487: 	}
488: 	if expected.HostDigest == "" || expected.BootID == "" || expected.BirthToken == "" || observed.HostDigest == "" || observed.BootID == "" || observed.BirthToken == "" {
489: 		return "owner_process_identity_incomplete_after_grace", TerminalCleanupUncertain
490: 	}
491: 	if expected.HostDigest != observed.HostDigest || expected.BootID != observed.BootID || expected.PID != observed.PID || expected.BirthToken != observed.BirthToken {

All primary paths inspected; hypotheses tested against callers, guards, and tests. Findings below, strongest first.

---

## F1 — TUI study-cancel accepts a *stale, unrelated* Confirmation into the durable spine (or none at all)

**Claim.** `ActionCancel`'s study branch builds a fresh `OperationStudyCancel` request but `beginOperation` gates durable acceptance on whatever `m.model.Confirmation` happens to hold, not on the request being run (`internal/tui/app.go:139` → `app.go:235-255`). `Confirmation` survives tab switches and forward navigation (`model.go` — only `ActionBack`, `OperationMsg`, and `beginOperation` clear it), so it is routinely stale when `c` is pressed.

**Observable bad outcomes.**
1. *False durable record + poisoned alias:* user prepares operation A (e.g. "Run Flow to plan"), navigates to a study with an active run, presses `c`. `AcceptOperation(opctx, *staleConfirmation, digest)` creates a run-control row with `Target.Operation = sprint-flow` (A's kind/scope) plus an alias row for A's content digest, while the code actually SIGINTs the study loop; `FinishOperation` then records that flow run "completed" (`durable_operations.go:99-105, 286-299`). Any later genuine TUI confirm of A hits `Existing` and is refused with "matching durable operation already exists" (`app.go:245-250`) until retention evicts the row — `operation_aliases` rows are never deleted (grep of `internal/runcontrol/sqlite.go`: insert at :449, no delete anywhere).
2. *Vocabulary bypass:* with `Confirmation == nil` the same keystroke skips `AcceptOperation` entirely — a mutating interactive action lands no durable row, contrary to user-guide.md:376-377 ("Every … confirmed web/TUI operation … receives a durable run before work starts") and to the web door, where `study-cancel` is fully prepared/confirmed/accepted (`operation_handlers.go` → `mapOperationRequest` :716-717, `PrepareOperation` :328-331).

**Trigger/preconditions.** TUI composition always satisfies `DurableOperationManager` (`tui_commands.go:52`); reachability is the advertised flow "view active study run, press c".

**Counter-evidence searched.** `setTab`, `LoadMsg`/`RefreshMsg`, `ActionOpen` route pushes — none clear `Confirmation`; the other two `beginOperation` callers (:104, :155) pass `Confirmation.Request`, so only this site breaks the pairing invariant.

**Severity:** high (durable-state falsification + blocking of legitimate operations). **Confidence:** high (static path unambiguous; no test covers `ActionCancel` × stale `Confirmation`).
**Regression test:** drive `teaModel.Update` with a planted `Confirmation` for kind X, fire `ActionCancel` on a study route with a fake manager recording accepted requests; assert accepted `Request.Kind == study-cancel` (or that acceptance is skipped), and that `ActiveOperation` equals the accepted request.

## F2 — TUI content-digest regime permanently forbids re-running identical operations, including state-dependent status refreshes

**Claim.** TUI dedup key = sha256(CanonicalRequest + "\x00" + InputFingerprint) (`app.go:236-238`) is inserted into an append-only table and resolved forever (`sqlite.go:449`, `ResolveOperationAlias` :472-484, no eviction). Identical confirmed content therefore maps to `Existing` for the lifetime of the database — including after the original run reached a terminal state.

**Observable bad outcome.** Run "Sprint Status" from the TUI; press Enter again on the re-prepared identical confirmation: `AcceptOperation` returns `Existing`, the TUI prints "matching durable operation already exists" and performs **no work** (`app.go:245-250`). Yet the status result legitimately changes because its outputs depend on `.run-state.json`/flow-state/smoke-review facts that `governedOperationInputs` does **not** hash for non-QA kinds (`operations.go:663-686` — `.run-state.json` added only for `qa-*`), so the operator is served a silently frozen answer. Same block applies to re-running flows/QA dry-runs with unchanged governed inputs.

**Cross-door parity break.** Web binds identity to sha256(session+token) (`security.go:448-451`): every fresh prepare issues a new token, so identical content can be started unlimited times; CLI passes `""` (`durable_operations.go:55`): no dedup at all. One logical action, three incompatible durable identities landing in the same `confirmation_digest`/alias column — precisely the assignment's trust boundary, violated in the direction of "door determines whether you may act at all".

**Counter-evidence searched.** `TestDurableOperationDeduplicatesAcrossManagersAndFailsClosed` pins the mechanism, not the product semantics; no doc states identical content must be permanently un-re-runnable; web contract scopes replay to "the same accepted session/token" (local-web.md:137-138), i.e. in-flight only.

**Severity:** high (routine operations silently become unavailable on one of three doors). **Confidence:** high.
**Regression test:** app-level — accept+finish an operation with digest D, re-accept identical confirmation, assert a fresh run is created (or an explicit typed refusal with remediation); plus a TUI test that "Sprint Status" executes twice consecutively.

## F3 — Browser hub cancellation never persists `RequestCancellation`; cancellation state diverges across surfaces

**Claim.** For hub-owned durable operations, `cancelOperation` only flips the in-memory doc and cancels the context (`operations.go:347-374`); nothing calls `RequestCancellation` (grep: callers are CLI `run_commands.go:216`, TUI `app.go:110/124`, web *fallback* `operation_handlers.go:209/392`, `CancelQA` `sprint_usecases.go:993`). Terminal proposal then writes `terminal_reason="operation cancelled"` with `cancellation_state=none` and no cancellation/acknowledgement events in the journal (`lifecycle.go:70-134` untouched).

**Observable bad outcomes.**
- During the unwind window, `/api/v1/runs/{id}`, `run show`, `run follow`, and the TUI Runs view show `lifecycle=running, Cancellation: none` while `/api/v1/operations/{id}` shows `cancelling/user_request` — contradicting user-guide.md:377-380 ("The same ID, lifecycle, liveness, **cancellation state** … are shown on every surface").
- If the process dies in the window, the operator's cancel intent vanishes: startup reconcile marks the row `interrupted`/`cleanup_uncertain` (`lifecycle.go:340-412`) with no cancellation record or reason anywhere durable. Every other door survives that crash with `cancelling + reason` persisted first.

**Counter-evidence searched.** Manager control loop only *reads* `CancellationRequested` (`durable_operations.go:240-247`); drain intentionally skips it too, but drain has its own cleanup-uncertain protocol whereas interactive DELETE does not. Tests assert only hub-doc states (`operations_test.go:144-158`), no durable assertion.

**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high.
**Regression test:** full-stack HTTP test with real repository: start durable op, `DELETE /api/v1/operations/{id}`, assert within a tick `runs.Snapshot().Cancellation.State == requested` (fails today).

## F4 — TUI run-detail replay window never advances; runs with >200 events show only their oldest page forever

**Claim.** Every load/refresh/1 Hz tick fetches `RunEvents(ctx, id, OldestRetainedSequence−1, 200)` (`app.go:372-388`); `Events` returns ascending `sequence > after LIMIT n` (`sqlite.go:809-821`). The cursor is never advanced to the last seen sequence, so for any run exceeding 200 retained events (chatty flow/QA/study operations do within minutes), the rendered "Retained events" list (`views.go:335-342`) is permanently pinned to the oldest ≤200 events; progress, warnings, findings, artifacts, `cancellation`, and `terminal` events never appear while the header's `last=N` keeps growing.

**Counter-evidence searched.** `run follow` advances `after = event.Sequence` (`run_commands.go:174`); web SSE fallback advances identically (`operation_handlers.go:491`) — the triplicated logic diverged exactly here. `dedupeDurableEvents` keeps the tail *of what was fetched*, which is always the same head window. `run_view_test.go` fakes ignore the `after` argument, so tests cannot catch this.

**Severity:** medium (operator console blind to live durable state for long operations). **Confidence:** high.
